Ahead, a small building comes into view, its half-lit neon sign reading: CONEY ISLAND METHADONE CENTER. The camera drifts forward, passing through the double doors into the reception area, where people linger, filling out papers. Moving down a narrow hallway, the sound of singing grows louder—a guitar strumming, a voice rising. The camera pushes through another set of doors marked 'Treatment Room.' Inside, a large orange rhinoceros sits on a stool, strumming a guitar. It's Smoochy—Sheldon Mopes in costume, his painted face visible beneath the misshapen foam, a multicolored horn jutting from his forehead. He sings to the patients lined up before a sliding glass window, where a nurse hands each a small cup of methadone. They drink it quickly, some glancing at Smoochy as he sings in a cheerful tune: 'We'll get that monkey off your back, Yes we will, yes we will...' The song ends. A few patients clap, uncertain. 'Thanks, fellas. I'm rooting for you!' Smoochy says. The camera pans away toward the exit, where Nora stands in her coat, face flushed, looking on in silence.

description: The song ends and Sheldon, still seated in the bulky orange rhinoceros costume, smiles and says, 'Thanks, fellas. I'm rooting for you!' A few patients offer half-hearted applause. The camera moves toward the doorway, where Nora stands just outside the treatment room, wrapped in her coat. Her face is pale, her expression stunned, as she takes in the sight of Sheldon in the ill-fitting Smoochy costume, the guitar at his side, the painted face visible beneath the drooping foam.
related_events: Nora arrives at the treatment room exit looking mortified
related_occasions: Methadone Treatment Session At Coney Island Methadone Center

name: Men Chant 'Heil Smoochy' Under Swastika Banner
description: Several hundred men in Nazi uniforms stand in a warehouse adorned with swastikas. They chant 'Heil Smoochy! Heil Smoochy! Heil Smoochy!' in unison. A large swastika banner unfurls behind Smoochy, framing him as flashbulbs pop. German march music blares from the speakers, filling the space with a driving rhythm. The crowd continues chanting, their voices rising in unison as the music plays.
related_events: Men in Nazi uniforms chant 'Heil Smoochy' under a swastika banner
German march music blares from speakers at the rally

name: Sheldon Questions the Swastikas at the Rally
description: The music stopped, and the crowd fell silent as Sheldon stood at the microphone, his expression dazed. He cleared his throat and spoke, his voice carrying over the quiet warehouse. 'It's my sincere hope that I'm dreaming right now, but in the event that I'm not... what's the deal with the swastikas?' His words hung in the air as the men in Nazi uniforms remained still, the swastika banner still draped behind Smoochy.
related_events: Sheldon speaks into the microphone after the music stops

name: Police Raid the Smoochy Rally
description: A group of policemen burst into the warehouse, shouting that the gathering is an unlawful assembly. The lead cop declares all attendees under arrest, calling them 'kraut sons-a-bitches.' Immediately, the men in Nazi uniforms scatter in panic, running in all directions to escape. Amid the chaos, Sheldon stands frozen in place, motionless as the crowd disperses around him.
related_events: Policemen storm the warehouse and declare the rally an unlawful assembly
Nazi rally participants flee in panic after police raid
Sheldon remains immobilized during the police raid on the rally

name: Randolph Confronts Stokes at the Dock
description: Randolph paces on a deserted dock beneath an awning, the Brooklyn Bridge looming in the distance. A car pulls up behind him, and Stokes steps out. Randolph steps forward, flask in hand. He asks if Stokes was really at a dinner engagement, then launches into a bitter recollection of his past fame and influence. His voice rises as he recalls the adoration he once received, shouting that he was 'Rainbow fucking Randolph.' Stokes tells him to stop, but Randolph grabs his lapels, pleading for his job back and accusing Stokes of abandoning the man who made his success possible. Stokes pries Randolph’s hands away and tells him he can do nothing—Randolph is a pariah, and the network now demands a clean image. He asks if Randolph is completely broke, then warns him never to contact him again. Stokes walks off into the mist. Randolph shouts after him, vowing revenge on both Stokes and the man who replaced him. Alone, he takes a swig from the flask, wipes his chin, and stares at the river as thunder rumbles overhead.
related_events: Randolph confronts Stokes on a deserted dock
Stokes arrives at the dock after a dinner engagement

name: Randolph Recalls His Glory Days on the Dock
description: Randolph paces on a deserted dock beneath an awning, the Brooklyn Bridge looming in the distance. A car arrives and Stokes steps out. Randolph approaches, flask in hand, and takes a swig before speaking. He speaks of his past life—fine dinners, luxury cars, horses, and the adoration of crowds. He remembers how people would scramble at his presence, how restaurants would hush when he entered. His voice rises as he declares himself 'Rainbow fucking Randolph,' a man once at the center of it all. He pleads with Stokes, clutching his coat, begging for his position back, insisting he’s broke, homeless, and hunted by bookies. Stokes pulls away, cold and unmoved, telling Randolph he can do nothing and warning him never to contact him again. Alone, Randolph stares out at the river, wipes his mouth with his sleeve, and mutters into the night that even the clean will eventually fall into the mud. Thunder cracks overhead.
related_events: Randolph recalls his past fame and excess
Randolph drinks from his flask and reflects on his situation

name: Randolph Pleads for His Job Back
description: Randolph's voice trembled as he grabbed Stokes by the lapels, his eyes wide with desperation. He begged for his position to be restored, speaking of being evicted from the corporate penthouse, owing money to bookies, and having nowhere to live. Stokes stood still, then pried Randolph's hands away from his coat before stepping back.
related_events: Randolph breaks down and pleads for his position to be restored
Randolph confesses his desperate situation to Stokes
Stokes pries Randolph's hands from his overcoat

name: Stokes Rejects Randolph, Who Vows Revenge
description: Stokes meets Randolph on a deserted dock beneath an awning, where Randolph pleads for his job back, clutching at Stokes' coat. Stokes pries his hands away and tells him he can do nothing, that Randolph is now a pariah and they can no longer be seen together. He walks off into the mist, ignoring Randolph's desperate calls. Alone, Randolph raises his flask and shouts after him, vowing that both Stokes and the rhino will get what they deserve. Thunder cracks as he turns toward the river, whispering to himself that even the cleanest man will eventually fall into the mud.
related_events: Stokes refuses to help Randolph and ends their relationship
Randolph threatens revenge on Stokes and the rhino

name: Randolph Tells of His Fall
description: Randolph sits at the kitchen table with Angelo, eating a bowl of soup. He points to a swollen bump near his eye, saying he was kicked out of the corporate penthouse. He pulls back his lip to show a missing tooth, blaming network security after a visit to the studio. As he speaks, he grows more agitated, listing liens, back taxes, lawyer's bills, and threats against his life. He laughs, mimicking an old dialect, and takes a long swig from a bottle of gin. His voice rises as he rants about revenge, then suddenly passes out, collapsing off the chair. Angelo leans down, lifting Randolph's head from the floor and slapping his face, urging him to stop destroying himself. Half-conscious, Randolph mutters that the rhino is the face of evil, sent from hell to destroy him.
related_events: Randolph recounts being evicted from corporate penthouse
Randolph reveals injury from network security confrontation
Randolph expresses financial and personal distress
Randolph drinks gin after emotional outburst

name: Randolph Spits Bay Leaf on the Floor
description: Randolph sits at the kitchen table eating soup. As he slurps a spoonful, he spits a bay leaf onto the floor.
related_events: Randolph discards bay leaf on floor while eating soup

name: Randolph Passes Out, Angelo Tries to Revive Him
description: After drinking heavily from a bottle of gin, Randolph loses consciousness and collapses off his chair onto the floor. Angelo kneels beside him, lifts his head, and slaps his face in an attempt to wake him. Randolph stirs slightly but does not respond.
related_events: Randolph passes out and falls off chair
Angelo lifts Randolph's head off the floor
Angelo slaps Randolph's face to revive him

name: Randolph's Delirium About Smoochy the Rhino
description: After collapsing from exhaustion and drink, Randolph lies on the kitchen floor, barely conscious. As Angelo leans over him, Randolph stirs slightly and mutters in a strained voice that the rhino, Smoochy, is a creature sent by the devil from hell to destroy him.
related_events: Randolph speaks delusionally about rhino being sent by devil

name: Irish Dancers Perform in a Dark Club
description: The camera focuses on the feet of an Irish dancer, moving rapidly in precise rhythm. The frame widens to reveal a full line of dancers performing a synchronized routine in the style of Riverdance, their steps sharp and thunderous against the floor. The performance unfolds in a dimly lit club, where Spinner and a group of onlookers clap and whoop with excitement, their voices rising over the music. The dancers continue their choreography, met with steady applause and cheers from the crowd.
related_events: Irish dancers perform a Riverdance-style routine in a dark club
Spinner and the mob react enthusiastically to the dance performance

name: Sheldon Rejects the Ice Show Deal
description: In a dimly lit club, Sheldon and Burke sit at a booth, deep in conversation. Burke leans forward, laying out the benefits of an ice show, talking about the money and power it could bring. Sheldon listens, then shakes his head, saying he never agreed to such a thing. He calls ice shows mindless spectacles that profit from overpriced drinks and cheap toys that break in children's mouths. Burke urges him to set aside his principles, insisting no one turns down an opportunity like this. Without a word, Sheldon takes the contract and tears it in half. He says Smoochy doesn’t sell out, and that Burke should be proud to represent someone who paves driveways, not paints them over. Burke sits frozen, stunned. A waitress, Sandy, passes by. Sheldon asks for pineapple juice. She hesitates, asking what happened to orange juice. He replies that he’s feeling feisty tonight.
related_events: Burke pitches the financial benefits of the ice show venture
Sheldon expresses opposition to participating in an ice show
Sheldon tears up the contract and declares his refusal to sell out

name: Sheldon Orders Pineapple Juice
description: After tearing the contract in half, Sheldon sits quietly for a moment. A waitress, Sandy, passes by the booth. He looks up and says, 'I'll have a pineapple juice, Sandy.' She pauses and asks, 'Pineapple? What happened to orange juice?' Sheldon replies, 'I'm feeling feisty tonight.'
related_events: Sheldon orders pineapple juice instead of his usual orange juice

name: Sheldon interrupts Nora's phone call and asks to talk
description: Sheldon enters the room while Nora is on the phone. He waits without speaking, looking around at small objects and photos on the wall. After a moment, he leans in slightly and silently mouths that he needs a moment of her time. Nora, still on the phone, tells the caller she’ll call back, saying someone is bothering her. She hangs up. Sheldon apologizes, saying she didn’t have to end her call. Nora replies that if she hadn’t, he would still be waiting. Sheldon says he wants to start on the right foot, that he values her input, and sees her as a partner. Nora responds sarcastically, saying that will be useful if they’re ever at a square dance. Sheldon offers to take her to lunch sometime to talk and build mutual respect. Nora says no. Sheldon says he understands and that she can change her mind. She says she won’t. He nods and walks toward the door. As he passes a plant, he glances at it and says, 'Ficus?' Nora does not respond. He leaves.
related_events: Sheldon silently interrupts Nora's phone call
Nora hangs up the phone after complaining about Sheldon
Sheldon apologizes for causing Nora to hang up

name: Sheldon Tries to Make Peace with Nora
description: Sheldon waits while Nora finishes her phone call, passing the time by looking at objects in the room. When she hangs up, he tells her he just needs a moment of her time. She responds sharply, saying she hopes to make his departure happen soon. Sheldon says he wants them to start off on the right foot, that he values her input, and considers her a partner. Nora replies sarcastically, saying that might help if they’re at a square dance. Sheldon ignores the sarcasm and invites her to lunch, describing it as a chance for colleagues to talk and build mutual respect. Nora says no. Sheldon says it’s fair, and adds that the offer stands if she changes her mind. She tells him she won’t. He nods, turns, and leaves. As he passes the door, he glances at a plant and says, 'Ficus?' Nora does not respond. He exits.
related_events: Sheldon attempts to establish a collaborative relationship with Nora
Nora expresses desire for Sheldon to leave

name: Sheldon Asks Nora to Lunch, Nora Declines
description: Sheldon tells Nora he would like to take her out to lunch, describing it as a chance for two colleagues to talk, build mutual respect, and start working together. Nora responds with a clear 'No.' Sheldon says it's fair and adds that the offer stands if she changes her mind. Nora replies that she won't. Sheldon nods, then leaves, mentioning he’ll be in his office if she needs him. As he passes a plant by the door, he mutters, 'Ficus?' Nora ignores him. He exits.
related_events: Sheldon suggests taking Nora out to lunch to build a collegial relationship
Nora rejects Sheldon's lunch invitation

name: Sheldon Leaves After Rejection
description: After Nora refuses Sheldon's lunch invitation and says she won't change her mind, Sheldon nods, says he'll be in his office if she needs him, and mentions she can come by to brainstorm ideas. As he leaves, he pauses by a plant near the door and says, 'Ficus?' Nora does not respond. He exits, and she remains at her desk.
related_events: Sheldon offers to collaborate with Nora in his office
Sheldon identifies a plant as a ficus while leaving Nora's office

name: Husband and Wife Offer Bribe to Rainbow Randolph in Bar
description: A suburban-looking husband and wife enter a bar and approach Rainbow Randolph, who is sitting alone, drinking a Scotch. His hair is slicked back, and he looks less friendly than before. The couple sits down nervously. The husband places a briefcase on the table and slides it toward Randolph. Randolph takes a sip of his drink, opens the briefcase, and sees the money inside. The husband stammers, asking that his son be placed at the front during the show for maximum camera time. Randolph slams the briefcase shut, startling them. He tells them not to tell him how to run his business. The couple stammers apologies, saying they only want their son on the show. Randolph stands, finishes his drink, picks up the briefcase, and says he’ll call if a spot opens up. He turns and starts to walk away.
related_events: Husband and Wife approach Rainbow Randolph in a bar
Husband presents briefcase to Rainbow Randolph
Husband requests preferential treatment for his son on the show

name: Rainbow Randolph Inspects the Bribe and Ends the Meeting
description: Rainbow Randolph and a suburban couple sit at a table in a bar. The husband places a briefcase on the table and slides it to Randolph. Randolph opens the case, looks at the money inside, then slams it shut. He drinks from his glass of Scotch and stands up. The husband stammers that they want their son to dance up front, where he’ll get the most camera time. Randolph cuts him off, telling them not to tell him how to run his business. The couple stammers apologies, saying they only wanted their child on the show. Randolph takes another drink, picks up the briefcase, and says he’ll call if a spot opens up. He turns and starts to walk away.
related_events: Rainbow Randolph inspects the contents of the briefcase
Rainbow Randolph rejects the couple's demands and ends the meeting

name: Husband and Wife Draw Guns on Rainbow Randolph
description: After Randolph turned and began to walk away, the Husband and Wife suddenly stood up and pulled out guns. The Husband shouted, 'Freeze, you cocksucker!' while the Wife demanded, 'Drop the briefcase!'
related_events: Husband and Wife draw guns and threaten Rainbow Randolph

name: Federal Agents Confront Rainbow Randolph in Bar
description: Federal agents burst into the bar and quickly surround Rainbow Randolph as he stands with a briefcase in hand. The Husband and Wife, who had drawn their guns and ordered him to freeze, remain on their feet, now caught in the agents' perimeter. The room falls tense as the agents secure the scene, weapons trained and commands issued.
related_events: Federal agents raid the bar and surround Rainbow Randolph

name: Randolph Sabotages Smoochy's Magic Cookie Bag
description: Randolph sneaks into the prop room and shuts the door behind him. He moves quickly to the prop shelf, finds Smoochy's multicolored magic cookie bag, and opens it. He dumps the cookies inside into a nearby trash can. From his pockets, he pulls out a batch of homemade cookies and pours them into the bag. Holding the bag, he says, 'Bon soir, la Smoochy. Welcome to fatty Arbuckle-land,' and laughs. In the corner of the room, he notices a box marked with 'Rainbow Randolph crap' in magic marker. He pulls it out, opens it, and removes his old costume. He holds it close, sniffing it. After a moment, he places the costume into his duffle bag and zips it up.
related_events: Randolph sneaks into the prop room and shuts the door
Randolph replaces Smoochy's magic cookies with homemade cookies
Randolph mocks Smoochy with a taunting greeting

name: Randolph Finds His Old Costume
description: Randolph moves through the prop room and spots a box in the corner, marked in magic marker with the words 'Rainbow Randolph crap.' He pulls the box out and opens it. Inside, he finds his old costume. He takes it out and holds it closely, pressing it against him. He brings the fabric to his face and inhales. For a moment, the sound of his theme song echoes as if from a distance, accompanied by the laughter of children. He places the costume into his duffle bag and zips it up.
related_events: Randolph discovers a box labeled with his discarded belongings
Randolph retrieves and emotionally reacts to his old costume
Memory of Rainbow Randolph's theme song and children's laughter echoes

name: Randolph's Vow and Departure
description: Randolph stands in the dim light of the prop room, holding Smoochy's magic cookie bag. He speaks softly, as if to unseen children, saying not to worry because Rainbow Randolph will return. His voice grows sharper, more forceful, as he adds that his return will come after these messages. He lifts the cookie bag high, then turns and places it aside. Walking back to the corner, he reaches into a cardboard box labeled with marker, pulls out his old costume, and holds it close. After a moment, he stuffs it into his duffle bag, zips it shut, and prepares to leave.
related_events: Randolph speaks to himself with soft reassurance and rising anger
Randolph holds up Smoochy's magic cookie bag
Randolph stuffs his old costume into his duffle bag

name: Sheldon's First Day in the New Office
description: Sheldon enters his new office and walks awkwardly to his desk. He sits behind it for the first time. Tommy, from Spinner Dunn's restaurant, speaks from across the room, surprising him. Tommy says his cousin Spinner has taken a liking to Sheldon since he started coming to the restaurant. Sheldon agrees that Spinner is a very nice man with a sweet disposition. Tommy asks if Sheldon could give Spinner a small part on the show, since he is now the executive producer. Sheldon hesitates, saying that television is complicated and compares the idea to getting into the ring with a prizefighter, laughing at the thought. Tommy grows quiet and says this makes him very sad. One of his crew asks who made him sad, but Tommy refuses to say. The men rise from the sofa and move around the desk, positioning themselves on either side of Sheldon. Sheldon quickly says he might be able to find something for Spinner on the show after all. Tommy smiles, walks over, and musses Sheldon's hair, calling him a good boy and saying they remember favors.
related_events: Sheldon enters and sits at his new office desk for the first time

name: Tommy Makes a Request in Sheldon's Office
description: Sheldon enters his new office and sits at his desk for the first time. He is startled when he notices Tommy from Spinner Dunn's restaurant standing in the room. Tommy is accompanied by his crew—Roy, Danny, Jimmy, and Sammy—who are seated on the sofa. Tommy says that his cousin Spinner has taken a liking to Sheldon since he started coming to the restaurant. He asks if Sheldon could give Spinner a small part on the show, noting that as executive producer, Sheldon has the authority to make that decision. Sheldon hesitates, saying it would be like him getting into the ring with a prizefighter, and laughs nervously. Tommy grows quiet and says this makes him very sad. Danny asks what’s wrong, and Sammy wants to know who made Tommy sad. Tommy avoids naming anyone, but the crew stands and moves around the desk, positioning themselves on either side of Sheldon. Sheldon quickly says he might be able to find something for Spinner on the show after all. Tommy smiles, walks over, and ruffles Sheldon’s hair, calling him a good boy and saying they remember favors.
related_events: Tommy surprises Sheldon by appearing in his office with crew
Tommy requests Sheldon to feature Spinner on the show

name: Sheldon Uses Humor to Decline Tommy's Request
description: Sheldon sits at his new desk when Tommy arrives with his crew. Tommy asks if Spinner, his cousin, can have a part on the show. Sheldon hesitates and responds with a joke, comparing the idea of putting Spinner on TV to himself getting into the ring with a prizefighter. He laughs, picturing himself knocked out, asking, 'What's the alphabet, Mommy?' Tommy grows quiet and says he is very sad. His crew stands and moves around the desk, positioning themselves on either side of Sheldon. Seeing their reaction, Sheldon quickly says he might be able to find Spinner something to do on the show after all. Tommy smiles, walks over, and ruffles Sheldon's hair, calling him a good boy.
related_events: Sheldon declines Tommy's request with a humorous analogy

name: Tommy and His Crew Intimidate Sheldon
description: Sheldon declines Tommy's request for his cousin Spinner to appear on the show. Tommy says this makes him sad, and his expression grows quiet. Danny asks what’s wrong, and Tommy replies that he’s just very sad. Sammy asks who made him sad, but Tommy avoids naming anyone. Roy, Danny, Jimmy, and Sammy glare at Sheldon and rise from the sofa. They move around the desk, positioning themselves on either side of him. Sheldon, now seated at his desk, quickly changes his mind and agrees to find something for Spinner on the show. Tommy smiles, walks over, and ruffles Sheldon’s hair before leaving.
related_events: Tommy expresses sadness and the crew reacts menacingly toward Sheldon

name: Sheldon Agrees to a Role for Spinner
description: Sheldon sits at his new desk when Tommy and his crew enter. Tommy mentions that his cousin Spinner has taken a liking to Sheldon and asks if Spinner could have a small part on the show. Sheldon initially declines, making a joke about being knocked out in a boxing match. Tommy grows quiet and says he is very sad, and the men rise and move around the desk, standing on either side of Sheldon. Sheldon quickly says he might be able to find a small role for Spinner after all. Tommy smiles, walks over, and ruffles Sheldon's hair.
related_events: Sheldon reverses his decision and offers to include Spinner on the show
Tommy accepts Sheldon's offer and affectionately ruffles his hair

name: Burke Confronts Frank Stokes Over Empty Warehouse
description: Burke tells Sheldon about the time he confronted Frank Stokes over a warehouse that was supposed to be full of unsold Dicky dolls. Knowing the warehouse in the Bronx was empty, Burke challenged Stokes and demanded proof. He went to the warehouse and found it as empty as he expected. Faced with the truth, Stokes wrote a check for a hundred thousand dollars. Burke left with the money while Stokes was left behind, defeated.
related_events: Burke confronts Frank Stokes about empty warehouse
Burke secures hundred-thousand-dollar check from Frank Stokes
Burke mocks Frank Stokes's failed business scheme

name: Burke Tells Sheldon About the Dicky Gimble Case
description: Burke and Sheldon sit at a corner table. Burke tells Sheldon about a time when his client, Dicky Gimble, had a dispute with Frank Stokes over unpaid merchandising money. Stokes claimed a warehouse was full of unsold Dicky dolls, but Burke knew the warehouse in the Bronx was nearly empty. He confronted Stokes directly, demanded to see the warehouse, and walked away with a check for a hundred thousand dollars. Burke laughs as he finishes the story. Sheldon says it’s amusing but insists he doesn’t care about merchandise—he wants more creative control over Smoochy. He slams his fist on the table, saying the character came from him and that he should have a say in how it’s raised. Burke finishes his drink, stands up, and says that money comes first, then power, and with power comes control. He hands Sheldon his card, tells him to call when he’s ready, and says he’ll cut the strings and open the magic door.
related_events: Burke recounts past legal dispute with Frank Stokes over merchandising

name: Sheldon Demands Control Over the Rhino Character
description: Sheldon sits at a corner table with Burke and speaks intensely about the rhino character, saying it came from his womb, that he bore it, nursed it, and should be the one to raise it. His voice rises with emotion, and he pounds his fist on the table.
related_events: Sheldon asserts creative ownership over the rhino character
Sheldon pounds fist on corner table in frustration

name: Burke Tells Sheldon How the Business Works
description: Sheldon and Burke sit at a corner table. Burke tells Sheldon that Frank Stokes isn't interested in making anyone rich except himself, explaining how people in the business operate. He recalls a story about his former client, Dicky Gimble, whose merchandising money Stokes tried to withhold by claiming a warehouse was full of unsold Dicky dolls. Burke says he knew the warehouse in the Bronx was empty, so he confronted Stokes directly. The encounter ended with Burke walking away with a hundred-thousand-dollar check while Stokes was left powerless. Burke laughs at the memory. Sheldon says it's sad and insists he doesn't care about Smoochy merchandise—he only wants more creative control over the character, which he feels is his creation. He pounds the table, declaring that he should be the one to raise the rhino. Burke replies that everything comes down to money, and once you have money, you gain power—enough to make Smoochy do anything you want. Sheldon says the idea never occurred to him. Burke finishes his drink, stands, and hands Sheldon his card, telling him to call when he's ready, promising to cut the strings and open the door for him.
related_events: Burke explains money and power dynamics to Sheldon
Sheldon expresses sadness about Frank Stokes's selfish motives

name: Burke Offers Sheldon a Way Out
description: Burke drains the last of his drink, rises from the table, and hands Sheldon his business card. He tells Sheldon to call him when he's ready, promising to cut the strings and open the door to a new path.
related_events: Burke finishes drink and prepares to leave meeting
Burke offers Sheldon a way out of creative subordination

name: Sheldon Gets Into the Limo With Merv and Henry
description: Sheldon slides into the back seat of the limo and finds himself seated between Henry, a large man in an overcoat, and Merv, who gets in right after him. The door shuts, and the limo drives down Broadway with Sheldon now wedged between the two men.
related_events: Sheldon enters limo and is seated between two men

name: Merv Introduces Himself and the Parade of Hope
description: Sheldon slides into the back seat of the limo and finds himself seated beside a large man in an overcoat. Merv gets in after him and closes the door. Merv extends his hand and says, 'Merv Green, Sheldon. It's a pleasure to meet you.' Sheldon responds with a nervous joke about autographs and guns. Merv introduces himself as a representative of the Parade of Hope Foundation. Sheldon acknowledges the organization, noting they build children's hospitals. Merv confirms this with a smile, and both he and the man beside him laugh.
related_events: Merv introduces himself to Sheldon
Merv reveals affiliation with Parade of Hope Foundation

name: Sheldon Confronts Merv in the Limo
description: Sheldon slides into the back seat of the limo and finds himself seated between Merv Green and a large thug in an overcoat. As the car pulls away, Merv extends his hand and introduces himself. Sheldon, visibly uneasy, responds with a nervous laugh, saying that if Merv wants an autograph, the gun seems excessive and that honey works better than vinegar when catching flies. Merv ignores the remark and states he represents the Parade of Hope Foundation, asking if it's true Sheldon is pulling out of the ice show. Sheldon sighs and insists he never agreed to any ice show and that it's none of Merv’s concern. Merv replies that the foundation has sponsored every Kidnet ice show since 1964 and implies the arrangement is not to be challenged. Sheldon reiterates he’s not doing the show and asks to be let out. Merv then declares that starting the next day, Smoochy the Rhino will be performing for Parade of Hope at benefits, banquets, and fundraisers, and suggests Sheldon start looking for skates. He tells the driver to pull over, and once the car stops, the door opens and Sheldon is thrown out onto the street.
related_events: Sheldon makes sarcastic comment about needing a gun for autograph request

name: Merv Confronts Sheldon in the Limo
description: Sheldon slides into the back seat of a limo, where a large thug named Henry is already seated. Merv gets in after him, shutting the door and trapping Sheldon between them as the car pulls away. Merv introduces himself with a handshake, but Sheldon responds with a nervous joke about autographs and guns. Merv says he represents the Parade of Hope Foundation, and Sheldon acknowledges it as the charity that builds children's hospitals. Merv then asks directly if it's true that Sheldon is pulling out of the ice show. Sheldon sighs and insists he never agreed to any ice show and that it's none of Merv's concern. Merv replies that the Parade of Hope has sponsored every Kidnet ice show since 1964 and warns against going against tradition. Sheldon repeats that he’s not involved and asks to be let out. Merv ignores the request and declares that starting the next day, Smoochy the Rhino will be performing for Parade of Hope at benefits, banquets, and fundraisers. He tells the driver to pull over, then adds that Sheldon should start shopping for skates. The door opens, and Sheldon is thrown out of the limo onto the street.
related_events: Merv confronts Sheldon about rumors of withdrawing from ice show
Sheldon denies involvement in or knowledge of ice show

name: Merv Forces Sheldon Out of the Limo
description: Sheldon shakes his head and insists he will not do an ice show, telling the driver to let him out. Merv leans forward and declares that starting the next day, Sheldon will appear as Smoochy the Rhino for Parade of Hope at benefits, banquets, and fundraisers. He then tells the driver to pull over. The limo stops, the door opens, and Sheldon is thrown out onto the street.
related_events: Merv threatens Sheldon with involvement in Smoochy the Rhino campaign
Merv orders the driver to stop the limo
Sheldon is forcibly ejected from the limo

name: Sheldon Carries Smoochy's Remains Through Reception
description: Sheldon enters the reception area wearing his street clothes. He carries Smoochy's body draped over his shoulder on a hanger and holds a large shopping bag containing Smoochy's head. Nora sits in the reception area and watches as he walks in. She speaks to him, addressing him as Mr. Mopes. They exchange greetings, and Sheldon asks if she is a new patient. Nora replies that she is not and hands him her business card. Sheldon reads the card, reacts with surprise, and greets her enthusiastically. He then asks her if she is hungry.
related_events: Sheldon carries Smoochy's body and head through reception

name: Nora Compliments Sheldon After His Performance
description: Nora sits in the reception area as Sheldon emerges in his street clothes, carrying Smoochy's body on a hanger over his shoulder and a large shopping bag containing Smoochy's head. name: Nora's Unannounced Visit
description: Shortly after hanging up the phone, Sheldon hears his doorbell ring. He opens the door to find Nora standing there. She asks if she can come in, and he lets her enter. Nora appears unsteady, holding a pint of whiskey. Sheldon asks if she’s okay, and she admits she’s getting drunk because she’s not used to apologizing. As she stumbles slightly, Sheldon takes the whiskey from her hand. He suggests they get some air and leads her out onto the balcony.

Nora reveals she is drinking to cope with apologizing
Sheldon takes whiskey from unsteady Nora to help her calm down

name: A Balcony Confession
description: Sheldon led Nora out onto the balcony after she arrived with a pint of whiskey, unsteady on her feet. She admitted she was drinking to ease the discomfort of apologizing, and told him she regretted being harsh in their previous conversations. She said she had heard he was not going through with the ice show, and found that choice deeply admirable. Sheldon replied that he hadn’t told her because he didn’t want to ruin the pleasure she seemed to get from arguing with him. Nora looked down and said she had grown hardened over the years, that sincerity was often faked in their line of work, and it was hard to tell who was genuine. Sheldon agreed, then recited softly: 'Sometimes light is really dark, Sometimes crows can sing like larks. Sometimes Winter feels like Spring, Don't think you know everything.' Nora stared at him. 'Rickets the Hippo?' she asked. They shared their childhood connection to the show, surprised to find a mutual affection for the character. Sheldon mentioned Rickets had inspired Smoochy. Nora said it had inspired her career. Remembering the Klunky-Wunky dance, they both began to perform it, laughing at first, then stopping to look at each other. Sheldon leaned in and kissed her. He pulled back, stammering that it was a mistake, but Nora grabbed his head and pulled him into a passionate kiss.

name: Dancing to the Klunky-Wunky
description: Sheldon and Nora stand on the balcony, looking out over the city. Nora mentions she may have been too harsh in their previous conversation. Sheldon jokes that it wasn’t as bad as the time she called him a pasty-faced, no-talent hack. She admits that was insensitive too. When Nora says she heard he’s not doing the ice show and finds that admirable, Sheldon says he didn’t want to spoil her fun. Nora reflects that she’s become hardened over the years, and sincerity is hard to come by. Sheldon agrees, then recites a few lines from the theme song of 'Rickets the Hippo.' Nora stares at him, surprised. 'Rickets the Hippo?' she says. They both confirm they remember the show, and how much it meant to them—Sheldon as the inspiration for Smoochy, Nora as the reason she went into children’s television. They laugh in disbelief at discovering this shared past. Sheldon asks if she remembers the Klunky-Wunky dance. Nora replies she did it at her first communion. They begin dancing together, mimicking the ridiculous moves. When they stop, they look at each other. Sheldon leans in and kisses her. He pulls back, apologizing, saying it was a mistake. Nora grabs his head and pulls him into another kiss. As they kiss, she murmurs, 'You’re not full of shit like all the others, are you?'
related_events: Sheldon and Nora recall shared childhood memories of Rickets the Hippo
Sheldon and Nora perform the Klunky-Wunky dance together

name: Sheldon and Nora Share a Kiss on the Balcony
description: After dancing together on the balcony, Sheldon leans in and kisses Nora. He immediately pulls back, apologizing and calling it a mistake. Nora responds by grabbing his head and pulling him into a passionate kiss. They kiss intensely, standing on the balcony overlooking the city. Without warning, Nora breaks the kiss, steps back, and says she is leaving. Sheldon asks why she is suddenly going, but Nora does not answer. She simply declines further conversation, says good night, and walks out. Alone again, Sheldon pours himself a glass of orange juice just as the phone begins to ring.

name: Sheldon Receives a Suspicious Invitation from a Fake Charity
description: After Nora leaves, Sheldon receives a phone call from Randolph, who is lying in bed in Angelo's apartment wearing a bathrobe. Randolph pretends to be Benjamin Kunklepeck from an organization called Parents for Decency in Children's Television. He tells Sheldon he has been selected to perform at a banquet and receive a plaque from a young orphan with mild asthma. The event is presented as a formal honor, though the call originates from within the city and is not what it appears to be.

name: Sheldon Eats a Soy Dog and Shares a Childhood Memory at Nathan's
description: Sheldon and Nora stand at the counter of Nathan's, surrounded by the lunchtime crowd. Sheldon eats a messy soy hot dog, talking with his mouth full about how he never thought he'd see the day when soy dogs would exist. He jokes about feeling bad for the beans, then launches into a story about how people always tell him to network and sell himself, but he believes in doing good work with integrity instead. He pulls the worn Smoochy the Rhino head from a shopping bag and holds it up, saying it represents concrete values, not empty promises. His voice rises, and he apologizes when he realizes he's speaking too loudly. He tells Nora he was raised by his grandfather, who painted driveways black to make them look paved, but the paint washed away in the rain. Sheldon says he vowed never to make a living through deception. Nora listens quietly, then tells him she’s at Nathan's because Kidnet is looking for a performer with convictions—someone like him. Sheldon laughs, thinking she’s joking, but when he sees she’s serious, he grows excited, asking if Kidnet is finally ready for a show of Smoochy’s quality. Nora confirms it, dryly. Sheldon declares they’re going to make history. The scene shifts to a montage at the Kidnet studio, where designers and seamstresses work on a new Smoochy costume, cutting orange foam rubber and fitting it around Sheldon as he stands on a wooden box. Blueprints labeled 'Smoochy the Rhino -- REDESIGN' hang on the wall. Sets and props begin to fill a studio, and signs appear, reading 'IT'S ALMOST SMOOCHY TIME!' and 'GET READY TO BE SMOOCHED, AMERICA!' The Smoochyland Magic Jungle set takes shape through a series of evolving scenes.

name: Sheldon Receives an Offer at Nathan's
description: Sheldon and Nora stand at the counter of Nathan's, surrounded by the lunchtime crowd. Sheldon eats a brightly colored soy hot dog with enthusiasm, talking through bites about his principles and how he refuses to compromise his integrity for fame. Nora watches quietly, then tells him that Kidnet is looking for a performer with real convictions—someone like him. Sheldon laughs, thinking it's a joke, but when Nora remains serious, he stops and stares at her. His expression shifts from disbelief to realization. He asks if she means it, and when she confirms, he grins widely. He says he always knew this day would come, that someone would finally understand what he stands for. He tells her she gets him, and she replies, 'I'm afraid so.' Sheldon, energized, calls her 'Miss V.P. of Development' and declares they should go make history. The scene shifts to a montage: designers cut orange foam rubber in a wardrobe room, a blueprint labeled 'Smoochy the Rhino -- REDESIGN' hangs on the wall, and Sheldon stands on a wooden box as a new Smoochy costume is fitted onto him. Sets are assembled, cameras rolled into place, and the jungle world of Smoochyland takes shape around the studio.

name: Sheldon Presents the Redesigned Smoochy Costume and Prepares for Taping
description: A seamstress zips up the final seam on the newly redesigned Smoochy costume, its bright orange foam rubber now shaped into a smooth, vibrant, and polished form. Sheldon steps down from the wooden platform, turns to face the design team, and strikes a pose, arms wide, beaming with pride. The team claps softly as he spins, showing off the finished suit. Nearby, in the bustling backstage area, Sheldon—now in full Smoochy attire—joins the Rhinettes, including Angelo, who adjusts his own costume and checks his microphone. Stagehands signal the performers; the studio lights brighten, and the group moves toward the curtain, ready for the taping to begin.

name: Smoochy Leads the Rhinettes in the 'Fantabulous Day' Performance
description: A choreographer directs a dance routine for Smoochy and the Rhinettes in a brightly lit studio. Nora and Stokes stand to the side, watching the rehearsal in silence, their expressions uneasy. Later, on the fully realized Smoochyland set, stage lights flare to life. An announcer calls out to the audience, and children shout back with excitement. Smoochy steps forward, waves to the crowd, and joins the Rhinettes—including Angelo Pike—in a lively performance of 'It's a Fantabulous Day in Smoochyland,' the music filling the studio as cameras roll.

description: At Kidnet Studio, Sheldon stands on a wooden box while a team of designers and seamstresses measure him from head to toe. They cut and shape sheets of orange foam rubber, assembling the new Smoochy the Rhino costume around him. A costume designer approaches with the updated Smoochy head and places it over his. name: Building the Smoochyland Set
description: Inside the Kidnet studio, workers haul in sets, props, and camera equipment, assembling them piece by piece. The Smoochyland Magic Jungle takes shape under bright lights—vines are hung, trees are painted, and pathways are laid. Through a series of gradual transitions, the set grows more detailed and complete, filling the studio space. Around it, crew members adjust lighting, test camera angles, and move equipment into position. The studio buzzes with activity as the set nears readiness for filming.

name: Smoochy Welcomes Angelo to the Rhinettes
description: Before the taping begins, Smoochy approaches Angelo near the set entrance. He extends his hand and offers a warm greeting, recognizing him as a former Krinkle Kid. Smoochy speaks of the 'Jellybean Jam' with genuine appreciation, praising Angelo’s performance from years past. He then invites Angelo to join the Rhinettes, welcoming him as a valued member of the current show. Angelo nods, accepting the role, as the crew moves into position for rehearsal.
